description: You are an agricultural economist at the Iowa Department of Agriculture conducting the 2022 Corn Yield Gap Analysis for state extension services. The workbook 'iowa_corn_yield.xlsx' on your Desktop (ExcelTasks folder) contains two sheets. 'County_Data' has 22 Iowa counties with 2022 actual corn yields (from USDA NASS county estimates), ISU Extension district attainable yield benchmarks as potential yields, and 2022 harvested acreage. 'Yield_Gap_Analysis' has county names (col A), actual yield (col B), potential yield (col C), and harvested area (col D) pre-filled; columns E through G and row 24 are blank. Complete the 'Yield_Gap_Analysis' sheet as follows: (1) Column E 'Yield Gap (%)': For each county, compute (Potential - Actual) / Potential × 100. (2) Column F 'Category': Use an IF formula — 'High Gap' if Yield Gap % >= 13, 'Low Gap' if Yield Gap % < 9, otherwise 'Medium Gap'. (3) Column G 'Rank': Use Excel's RANK function to rank each county from 1 (smallest gap, most efficient) to 22 (largest gap, least efficient) — rank in ascending order of Yield Gap %. (4) In cell E24 (labeled 'State Area-Weighted Avg Yield Gap:'): Use SUMPRODUCT to compute the harvested-area-weighted average yield gap: =SUMPRODUCT(D2:D23, E2:E23) / SUM(D2:D23). Save the completed workbook using Ctrl+S.

metadata.dataset: Real 2022 Iowa county corn yields from USDA NASS (Feb 24 2023); ISU Extension district benchmarks for potential yields
